## Method and scope

`git merge-base --is-ancestor <candidate-tip> opus/spellcheck` returned 0 for all eight. Tracked changes use `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=no`. Untracked and ignored inventories use separate NUL-delimited `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` queries, with `--ignored` for the latter. Counts include symbolic links as entries; bytes are logical lstat bytes, not allocated disk space. Symlinks are not dereferenced or charged for their external targets. Full relative inventories and cache exclusions are in `artifacts/wt1/census.json`.

Citations: offline `rg --json -n -I --hidden --no-ignore`, scanning every nonbinary text file under the six roots below (a superset of docs/configs/scripts/deploy manifests/receipts). `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, and this WT1 report/census directory are excluded. Both absolute prefixes and `~/Projects/` spellings are searched with a worktree-name boundary, avoiding l1/l1r prefix collisions. Every matching file and line is listed below; exact source lines and per-occurrence targets are retained in JSON. No hit is waived as historical: receipts and archives are conservatively treated as live until the lead rules. Binary files and symlink-directory traversal are outside this text grep.

## Lead script contract and ruling format

Run `bash docs/records/reviews/harness/wt_remove_20261017.sh --dry-run --ruling artifacts/wt1/WT1_RULING.placeholder.json` for the empty placeholder. Default mode is dry-run. Execution always reads the lead-owned `docs/records/reviews/harness/WT1_RULING.json`; alternate rulings are accepted only for dry-run. Logs use the same scratchpad as the merge script, with timestamp plus a unique suffix.

The ruling binds `main_tip` and `census_sha256`; each REMOVE entry binds name, branch, tip, and custody/repoint booleans. Empty `worktrees` authorizes nothing. Names outside the exact eight, drift, tracked changes, process cwd, missing/nonidentical replacements, or remaining citations fail closed. KEEP entries never remove. Only listed REMOVE entries reach `git worktree remove <path>`.

Custody preserves all untracked AND ignored entries except the two explicitly regenerable cache classes. It preserves relative paths and symlink objects without following their targets, hashes regular-file contents or symlink target bytes, verifies each copy, and writes `<name>.sha256.json` beside the custody directory. Existing destinations/manifests are refused. Originals remain untouched. **Non-ignored untracked files therefore cause ordinary Git removal to refuse, even after custody; the script aborts without retry.** The lead must separately resolve that refusal under a new explicit ruling/workflow; this script does not silently delete originals. Ignored-only caches/evidence may be discarded by ordinary Git removal, which is why ignored evidence is also copied first.

Every citation in the census must have a verified identical replacement and be repointed before removal. Directory-only, missing, dynamic, changed, or shell-variable paths are explicitly unresolved below. No replacement is asserted for those. A separate verified custody-based replacement can be proposed by the lead after custody; this snapshot must then be refreshed and re-bound. The script never edits citations.
